title: Adult striped mittens
subtitle: Full mittens in two-colour stripes, worked in the round in DK wool.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Full mittens in two-colour stripes worked in the round in DK wool, with an
afterthought thumb
. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.

Even-number stripes (such as the 4-round stripe used here) let you carry both yarns up the inside of the work rather than cutting and rejoining at every colour change. The unused yarn wraps loosely around the active yarn every 2 rounds to keep it tidy inside. The construction uses
magic loop
on a long circular. Budget about 70 g of each colour (155 m / 170 yards each), both DK.
What you need

items.name: Colour A
items.qty: 70 g (about 155 m / 170 yards) of DK-weight wool

items.name: Colour B
items.qty: 70 g (about 155 m / 170 yards) of the same yarn in a contrasting colour

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 3: 1 for beginning of round, 1 for thumb, 1 for top shaping midpoint

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the afterthought thumb

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 28 rounds to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles.
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and cuff

Using colour A and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 40 (44, 48) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 8 rounds of 2x2 rib in A. Join B. Work 4 rounds 2x2 rib in B. Work 4 rounds 2x2 rib in A. Repeat until cuff measures 7 (8, 8) cm.
Stripe hand

Switch to stocking stitch, continuing the 4-round stripe sequence. Work 10 (12, 12) rounds. Place the afterthought thumb: work the first 10 (11, 12) stitches with waste yarn, slip back, and work in stripe pattern to end. Continue the stripe sequence for 22 (24, 26) more rounds.
Top shaping

Place a marker at the midpoint. Continue the stripe sequence throughout shaping. Decrease round: k1, ssk, knit to 3 before midpoint, k2tog, k1, SM, k1, ssk, knit to last 3, k2tog, k1. Plain round. Repeat until 8 stitches remain. Draw yarn through and close.
Thumb
Remove waste yarn and pick up 10 (11, 12) stitches above and below the gap. Work 14 (16, 16) rounds in the stripe sequence. Bind off.
Common faults
Carried yarn shows through on the outside: the wrap was pulled across too tightly. Carry the resting yarn loosely and keep it close to the inside fold of the magic loop only.
Stripe colours do not align on both mittens: the stripe sequence started on a different round. Begin both mittens on the same stripe colour at the cast-on.
Finishing
Weave in tails at each colour change on the wrong side.
Care
Hand wash in cool water. Wash each colour separately for the first wash if either colour is strongly saturated, to check for bleeding. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next
Narrowing the stripe to 2 rounds and adding a third colour gives a more complex striped look. The child striped mittens pattern uses the same construction at a smaller gauge.
